2 Definitions
For the purpose of this standard the following definitions apply. 2.1 manufacturing management. organization: Welding workshops or sites under the same technical and quality

2.2 welding coordination personnel: Personnel who have responsibilities in the manufacturing operation for welding and welding related activities and whose competence and knowledge has been demonstrated by e.g. training, education and/or relevant manufacturing experience. A welding coordinator 2.3 is a person carrying out one or more coordination tasks.

welding inspection:

Examining, testing and measuring of welding related matters.

3 Tasks and responsibilities
3.1 Quality related activities allocate quality-related tasks and responsibilities to welding coordination for special applications. Not all the items will necessarily apply to all system requirements and a selection should be made as appropriate, e.g. non-destructive testing, No. 1.8.2 of table 1 does not apply.

5 Technical knowledge
5.1

Generalforallwelding coordinationpersonnel
adequate technical knowledge

For all tasks assigned, welding coordination personnel shall be able to demonstrate to enable such tasks to be performed satisfactorily. The following factors should be considered: -- -- general technical knowledge; specialized technical knowledge relevant to the assigned theoretical knowledge, training and/or experience.

tasks. This may be attained

by a combination

of

The extent of required manufacturing experience, education and technical knowledge manufacturing organization and will depend on the assigned tasks and responsibilities.

should be decided

by the

5.2 5.2.1

Authorized General

welding

coordination

personnel

Authorized welding coordination personnel (see 3.2) should normally be allocated from one of the following groups. This will depend on the nature and/or complexity of the production. Adequate manufacturing experience need not necessarily be longer than 3 years. 5.2.2 Comprehensive technical knowledge supervising

Welding coordination personnel with full technical knowledge according to 5.1 for planning, executing, and testing of all tasks and responsibilities in welding fabrication (see annex A). 5.2.3 Specific technical knowledge

Welding coordination personnel where technical knowledge is sufficient for planning, executing, supervising and testing of the tasks and responsibilities in welding fabrication within a selective or limited technical field (see annex A). 5.2.4 Basic technical knowledge

Weldirm coordination Dersonnel where technical knowledae is sufficient for planning, exetiuting, supervising and tes~ing of the tasks"and responsibilities within a limited technical field involving only simple welded constructions (see annex A).

Annex A

(informative)
Recommendations on technical knowledge

The European Welding Federation (EWF) has, on a voluntary basis, prepared recommendations requirements for education, examination and certification of welding coordination personnel. The recommendations -- are stated in the following documents:

for minimum

European Welding Engineer DOC. EWF 02-409-93; European Welding Technologist DOC. EWF 02-41 O-93; European Weldina S~ecialist DOC."EWF 02-41 i-95. acceptable national

--

.

Welding coordination personnel fulfilling the requirements of these documents or holding qualifications may be considered to satisfy the relevant requirements of 5.2.2, 5.2.3 and 5.2.4.
